comments.comment: My notes, or a slightly detailed summary of this video:  RULES FOR TIME RESTRICTED FEEDING:  - Do not ingest any food in the first hour (at least) after waking. - Do not ingest any food 2-3 hours before bed time (or liquid calories). - WHEN you eat is as important as WHAT you eat. - 8 hours of sleep is ideal for maximum health-related fasting benefits.  THE IDEAL FEEDING WINDOW:  When is it best to fast? It is important to note that fasting does not begin as soon as you are finished eating, because you are still digesting. - It is best to extend the sleep fast into the morning, or start in the evening. - Having a 12:00pm - 08:00pm eating window is ideal for most social settings (family, etc). - It is better to select for example a 6 hour feeding window if your focus is 8 hours, 8 hours if your focus is 10, in order to maintain adherence (if that is a problem). - Short feeding windows (4-6 hours) are best for positive health and psychological effects, HOWEVER, it can have no change or an increase in body weight, due to overeating in that window.  PROTEIN CONSUMPTION & MUSCLE GROWTH:  - Muscle is more able to grow early on in the day, because of the expression of a certain "clock gene" (BMAL1) that regulates protein synthesis. - It is best to break the fast early in the day (after having fasted for at least 1 hour after waking) with protein, to express muscle growth.  HOW TO SHIFT YOUR EATING WINDOW:  - Transition period of 7 - 10 days. - Shift eating window by 1 hour a day, until you reach your desired window. - Eating window times must be regular every day, with no occasional changes. - Accelerating the rate at which you begin your fasting state, which is done through:    - Light walking or excercise 20 mins.    - Intense training later in the day can help decrease blood glucose and hasten the fasted state.  ADDITIONAL NOTES:  - Eating only every other day has the most significant weight loss effects, without major detrimental health effects. - Lemon and cinnamon have a blood glucose lowering effect. - A pinch of salt in water can help with the side effects of low blood sugar during your fast (light-headedness, shakiness, inability to focus). - Caffeine will cause you to lose water (diuretic effect) and with it sodium. - Inclusion of the sleep related fast into your fasting schedule is important for health benefits.

comments.comment: This is so interesting and even slightly empowering. From my teens through my thirties, it was constantly hammered that "breakfast is the most important meal of the day" and if I don't eat as soon as I wake in the morning I'm hurting my body (meal-shaming?). I have always naturally woke up not hungry until around 11:00-11:30. Sometimes I will feel physically nauseous at the thought of eating and have many times forced myself to eat breakfast if I knew my day wouldn't allow lunch. Now I can call it "intermittent fasting" and people don't look at me funny and feel the need to meal-shame me for skipping breakfast! Now that I'm 50 years old, I'm wondering how this factors into perimenopause and menopause and the effects on my hormones now.

I'm thinking about adjusting my feeding window the day before a big ride so I stop eating at 3 or 4p and then I can eat breakfast prior to my ride. Is it ok to shift the feeding window back and forth or is consistency important? Thanks!

comments.comment: From personal experience as a type 1 diabetic. When you take your first bite of food it takes about 30 minutes for digestion to move sugar into the blood and a healthy person would have normal levels within two hours after that first bite. If that makes sense so you aren't technically fasting from 12:30-2:30 ish and you would be breaking fast again 5:30-730ish. Of course what you eat will change how long it takes your body to absorb sugar
